prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No space elevator exists and none can be built with available materials, so the Main KPI of 1 working space elevator is unmet. The tether is the pacing item: ISEC estimates 60 to 100 GPa is required, an order of magnitude beyond current materials (https://isec.org/space-elevator-newsletter-2018-april), while the strongest carbon nanotube fibres reported reach about 8.2 GPa quasi-static and 14 GPa dynamic on short samples (https://english.imech.ac.cn/news/rp/202406/t20240624_665537.html). Obayashi keeps a 2050 concept and says current technology is not sufficient (https://www.sciencealert.com/japanese-company-plans-to-build-a-tower-into-space-by-2050), and the only orbital demonstration, STARS-Me, moved a 6 cm climber on a 10 m tether (https://www.space.com/42041-space-elevator-test-stars-me.html). Honest limit: the binding problem is materials science at kilometre scale; tasks restating ISEC or Obayashi architectures are known work, and only verifiable progress on tether material or a new architecture is new.
